### The elements meditation (practice)
"The internal earth element and the external earth element are both
just the earth element itself... 'This is not mine', 'I am not this',
'this is not my self'."
"Having seen thus with right wisdom, he becomes dejected with the earth
element, he detaches his mind from the earth element."

### The Bahiya training (the tersest practice)
"In the seen there will be just the seen... Thus should you train
yourself."
"The basic principle in this training seems to be the discipline to
stop short at bare awareness."

### The Talaputa aspiration
"When shall I weigh as equal all these Limitless things both internal
and external, twigs, grass, creepers and these aggregates?"
"It is at the stage of arahant-hood that the internal and the external
appear alike."

### The Adhimutta connection
"When one sees through wisdom, the world to be comparable to grass and
twigs."

---

### The razor simile (parāmasana vs sammasana)
"With the idea of sharpening the razor, if one grabs it tightly and
rubs it on the sharpening stone, it will only become blunt. Paramasana,
grasping, grabbing, is something like that."
"One has to hold the razor in a relaxed way, as if one is going to throw
it away. One holds it lightly, ready to let go of it at any time. But,
of course, with mindfulness. The wrist, also, is not rigid, but relaxed.
Hand is supple at the joints and easy to swing."
"First: up, up, up, then: down, down, down, and then: up down, up down,
up down. The third combined movement ensures that those parts of the
blade still untouched by the stone will also get duly sharpened."
"Inward, inward, inward — outward, outward, outward — inward outward,
inward outward. Or else: arising, arising, arising — ceasing, ceasing,
ceasing — arising ceasing, arising ceasing."
"It is in the same manner that the razor of insight wisdom has to be
whetted on the sharpening stone of the Satipatthanasutta."

### The four foundations: attending makes objects
"The fact that the mind-objects arise due to attention is noteworthy.
All the mind-objects mentioned in the fourth section of contemplation
arise when there is attention. And they go down when attention is not
there. In other words, attending makes objects out of them."

### The Upatissa/Assaji story (stream-entry on two lines)
"Formerly, as brahmin youths, they were known as Upatissa and Kolita.
These two young men once went to see a hill-top festival... Since by
then, their discerning wisdom was already matured, they suddenly
developed a dejection about the entertainment going on. The hill-top
festival, as it were, lost its festivity for them."
"When Upatissa met the Venerable Assaji Thera on his alms-round, he
begged

### Yoniso manasikara (radical attention) vs ayoniso
"There is a world of difference between them... But from the point of
view of realization, there is just a little difference. That spectrum of
the sun's rays in the dewdrop disappears with a very little shift in
one's perspective."

### The Nagasamala episode
"Once, on my begging round, I happened to look up to see a dancing woman,
beautifully dressed and bedecked, dancing to the rhythm of an orchestra
just on the middle of the highway. Just then, radical attention arose
from within me, the perils were manifest, and dejection took place, then
my mind got released."
"If a train of thoughts had got started up about that gem, even through
a wrong concentration, at whatever moment radical attention comes on the
scene, complete reorientation occurs instantaneously."

### The four postures (continued from Sermon 8)
"In whatever way his body is disposed, so he understands it."
"A meditator becomes aware, while attending to his postures, that he is
merely enacting a dumb show."

### Scan first, then act
"First of all one has to mindfully scan or scrutinize it... But based
on that scrutiny, the four right endeavours play their role in regard
to unskilful and skilful mental states."

### Specialize by temperament
"One comes to know one's strongpoint, where one's forte lies...
One might recognize chanda, desire or interest, as one's strongpoint...
Another might discover that his true personality emerges in the thick
of striving... One who belongs to the wisdom category is never tired of
investigation."

### The tool-kits taken up together
"These seven tool-kits are interconnected. From the satipaṭṭhāna
tool-kit, the sammappadhāna tool-kit comes out as a matter of course."

---

### The attention/inattention technique
"In order to eliminate one thing by inattention, attention to some
other thing is recommended. For the purpose of inattention to
something gross, attention to something subtle is taken up. But that is
not the end of it. Even that is expelled with the help of something
subtler."
"Here we have a wonderful technique, based on the twin principles of
pragmatism and relativity."

### The graded reflection (impermanence → renunciation states)
The same reflection on impermanence gives rise to happiness,
unhappiness or equanimity "according to the attitude taken up."

### The path taken like a razor
"The constituents of the path have to be taken up as one takes up a
razor for sharpening, ready to let go. Once the purpose is served,
they have to be given up."

### Middle way as systematic gradual effort
"By means of a mindful and systematic gradual effort, work out his
freedom... he has to strive — not struggle."
"Freedom from it can be won only by a subtle form of striving...
Avoiding the two extremes of stagnation and struggling, one has to
cross the flood going the middle way."

### The lotus practice (untainted in the midst)
"Just as a blue lotus, born in the water, rises well above the water
and remains unsmeared — so the Tathagata dwells detached from ten
things with a mind unrestricted."

### The taste practice
"He takes his food experiencing the taste, though not experiencing
any attachment to the taste."

### Yathabhuta nana dassana (knowledge and vision of things as they are)
"It is by offering a knowledge and vision of things as they are, in
place of those two views of existence and non-existence."
"He made known to the world the true knowledge and vision that name-and-
form is merely an image reflected on consciousness."

### The practice: see the reflection as reflection
"The eternalist, because of his narcissistic self-love, gets attached
to his own self image and lags behind... It is like the narcissistic
attempt to embrace one's own image in water out of self love."
"The annihilationist view leads to an attitude of escapism, like that
of one who is obsessed by his own shadow. One cannot outstrip one's
own shadow."
